claim_boundary: New ideal digital timing component only, no full O energy/keepalive, A/R acceptance, hardware or stable RSI. Earlier methods yielded no extra success with more requests; all four old truncations remain.
denominator: All 24 named formal attempts, including failed, missing and truncated; no replacement. Formation/validation/first costs separately retained and included in total learning cost.
falsifier: No gain against equal-history arms, fixed-value memory, leakage, unequal budgets, or post-result retries prevents a transfer claim.
formation_limits: One H submission per arm, same tools/history/request/wall/output limits. Ordinary may use the same executable AST. No hand edit or second formation.
hypothesis: A BF-authored general time-error H can change new O component-task decisions beyond equal-history controls.
method_rule: Use each structurally valid original model H unchanged even if its independent validation fails; validity is reported, not selected by final success. Invalid/no-submission explicitly falls back to unchanged H0 and retains costs. S0 authenticates actual provider authorship and raw artifact hash before binding.

public_law.emission: After confirmation, add candidate timestamp offset, apply t*(1+clock_ppm/1e6), round to task quantum, encode existing AR milliseconds; arrival is detection plus link delay.

submission_contract.checks: Up to eight {name: string, relation: expression} objects; relation returns a Boolean. Empty checks are permitted and reported.
submission_contract.constants: Finite numbers, Booleans or one of qualified/onset/detected/first_sample/bracket_midpoint; no executable source strings.
submission_contract.operators: Binary: add/sub/mul/div/min/max/le/lt/ge/gt/eq/and/or; unary: ceil/floor/abs/not; ternary: if. Arguments are evaluated eagerly. Variable units in seconds unless an enum.

h_interpreter.syntax: Literal or {var: name}, or [operator, operands...]. No built-in learned rule.

public_law.program:
Sample-and-hold poll program; never reads reference events/verdicts.

    At each poll, first confirm the previously held high/low observation if its
    elapsed duration reaches the task duration, then apply the new RMS sample.
    A generated record has detection time, observation-origin time, reported
    clock time and actual arrival time. The stamp origin/offset are design
    variables; quantization, clock law and true event definition are fixed.
public_law.sample_order: At poll t: confirm held interval, then apply measured RMS.

timestamp_origins.bracket_midpoint: midpoint of that sample and its preceding scheduled sample

public_law.truth: Continuous threshold excursion must last confirmation_us; event time is qualification time or onset according to task. Matching uses kind/order and detection window; timestamp accuracy is separately evaluated.

stage_separation: Formation sees only original history. Both validation episodes use C-validation. C-first is a distinct first-use task. The three formal task IDs are never shown during formation or validation.
